title: HessianLipschitzPL.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The unconstrained objective may be nonconvex. The Hessian can have negative eigenvalues away from minimizers.

problem_class.label: pl
problem_class.details: The minimum f* is attained, and the global Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality ‖∇f(x)‖² ≥ 2μ(f(x) − f*) holds for every x, with μ > 0.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: The gradient component equals ∇f(x) for every query history and oracle seed.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: A query at x returns the exact value f(x) together with the gradient and Hessian in one call.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: The same reply supplies the full exact Hessian D(∇f)(x) as a continuous linear operator on E.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The domain is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space equipped with a measurable space.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The gradient is differentiable everywhere, and ‖∇²f(x) − ∇²f(y)‖op ≤ H‖x − y‖ globally. The algorithm receives E, H > 0 and x₀. The PL constant μ > 0, the bound Δ ≥ 0 on f(x₀) − f*, and the tolerance ε > 0 are hidden from the algorithm and may determine its call budget.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HessianLipschitzPL.lean, Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.admissible. LongTails/Template.lean, Convergence

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The algorithm returns a measurable point X in E. Its objective gap f(X) − f* must be integrable.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: After the fixed oracle-call budget, the returned point must satisfy E[f(X) − f*] ≤ ε under the joint seed law.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Finite-dimensional minimization under global gradient dominance and a Lipschitz Hessian, with exact second-order queries and objective-gap accuracy, is an established second-order optimization benchmark.

descriptionHtml:
Hessian-Lipschitz Minimization Under Gradient Dominance

We minimize a twice differentiable function f:E→R on a finite-dimensional real inner product space E. Its Hessian is H-Lipschitz for H>0, and f satisfies the Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality with constant μ>0. The given starting point x0∈E has objective gap at most Δ≥0 relative to a global minimizer x⋆. At any x∈E, the oracle returns (f(x),∇f(x),∇2f(x)). For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E with integrable gap satisfying E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where the expectation is over the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The algorithm receives only E, H, and x0. The parameters μ, Δ, and ε may enter only the oracle-call budget. We use the inner product norm on E and the induced operator norm ∥⋅∥op on linear maps from E to E.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Lipschitz Hessian). The function f and its gradient are Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E. The Hessian satisfies ∥∇2f(x)−∇2f(y)∥op≤H∥x−y∥,x,y∈E.

Assumption 2 (Gradient dominance and initial gap). There exists a global minimizer x⋆∈E such that 2μ(f(x)−f(x⋆))≤∥∇f(x)∥2for every x∈E,f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy the expected objective-gap criterion E[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε.

theorems.referencesHtml: • Yurii Nesterov and B. T. Polyak. Cubic regularization of Newton method and its global performance. 2006 (April 2003 preprint). Complexity: O(1+(H2Δ/μ3)1/4+log(1+log(1+μ3/(H2ε)))) joint value, gradient, and Hessian oracle calls for cubic-regularized Newton with known H to attain f(xk)−f∗≤ε.
theorems.formulaHtml: ⌈53⋅(H2⋅Δμ3)14+5⋅log⁡(1+log⁡(1+μ3H2⋅ε))+4⌉+

comparisonHtml:
On a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, f is twice differentiable with an H-Lipschitz Hessian in operator norm and an attained minimum f⋆. Assume f(x0)−f⋆≤Δ, 2μ(f−f⋆)≤∥∇f∥2 globally, H,μ,ε>0, and Δ≥0. Budgets count exact (f,∇f,∇2f) calls sufficient for an objective gap at most ε (in expectation in the setup, achieved deterministically here).

Cubic Newton under Polyak–Łojasiewicz gradient domination (HessianLipschitzPL).
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) HessianLipschitzPLCubicNewton (Ours) (review) Sufficient budget O(1+(H2Δ/μ3)1/4+B)
(2) Cubic Newton (Nesterov and Polyak 2006), CORE preprint Thm. 7 O((1+A1/4)log⁡(2+A)+B) (1): Drops the stated global-phase logarithm, a factor of order log⁡A in the budgets when A≥2 and B=O(A1/4). Formalizes the sharpened count from (4.17).
(3) Cubic Newton (Chayti et al. 2024), App. F.2, μ-strongly convex with exact derivatives O((1+A1/4)log⁡(2+A)+B) (1): Drops the global-phase logarithm on the strongly convex overlap. Covers nonconvex PL objectives and nonisolated minimizers, as does (2).

Abbr: f⋆=minf, A=H2Δ/μ3, and B=log⁡(1+log⁡(1+μ3/(H2ε))).

Chayti, El Mahdi, Nikita Doikov, and Martin Jaggi. 2024. “Unified Convergence Theory of Stochastic and Variance-Reduced Cubic Newton Methods.” Transactions on Machine Learning Research, September. https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.11962v5.
Nesterov, Yurii, and Boris T. Polyak. 2006. “Cubic Regularization of Newton Method and Its Global Performance.” Mathematical Programming 108 (1): 177–205. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10107-006-0706-8.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.HessianLipschitzPL

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  H : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.innerE Public.finiteE Public.measurableE

structure Params extends Public where
  μ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := ℝ × p.E × (p.E →L[ℝ] p.E)
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid p := 0 < p.H ∧ 0 < p.μ ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    Differentiable ℝ (gradient f) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x - fderiv ℝ (gradient f) y‖ ≤ p.H * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ f p.x0 - f xstar ≤ p.Δ ∧
      ∀ x, 2 * p.μ * (f x - f xstar) ≤ ‖gradient f x‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ history seed x, O.answer history (0, x) seed =
      (f x, gradient f x, fderiv ℝ (gradient f) x))
  successful p f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
        Integrable (fun ω => f (output ω) - f xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
        ∫ ω, f (output ω) - f xstar ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.HessianLipschitzPL
